Simone, it is Javier Ruiz, from the business team in Madrid. I heard that legal wants three more weeks to review the property files in Campinas, and I need to be honest with you: my stakeholders are not happy. The board wants to close at the end of March, and New York has already accepted that date. So, before Thursday's deal committee, I need a compelling reason, not a list of everything that could go wrong. Tell me your rationale in two sentences. Show me evidence: dates, numbers, documents. And tell me what it costs us if we do not wait. I am not against you. In fact, your team has a good track record, and that gives you credibility with me. But the committee will only give you buy-in if the benefit clearly outweighs the delay. You have five minutes for your pitch. Use them well.

Okay. Five minutes, three parts. Here is my pitch for Thursday. The property files in Campinas have not been checked since two thousand and nineteen. That is my first reason, and I can back it up with the data room index. In addition, the target had a problem with the regulator two years ago, so its track record is not clean. What is more, the antitrust clearance will take about ninety days anyway, so three weeks of review does not move the closing date at all. Therefore, I am asking for three more weeks, with a clear deadline and one person responsible. And the cost of not waiting? If there is a hidden liability in those files, our exposure is the whole value of the deal. The cost of three weeks does not outweigh that. One more thing: I am not going to say the risk is huge. It is not. It is small, but it is serious, and I have the evidence on one page.

First, you think about each stakeholder and what they are afraid of losing. Then, you choose one or two clear reasons, and that is your rationale. After that, you find evidence to back up each reason: a date, a number or a document. Next, you add the second reason with in addition, or with what is more. Finally, you finish with the request, as a result of the reasons: therefore, I am asking for it.
